title: North Bay cop recounts Couvrette turning "three colours" and yelling "satanic" stuff
subtitle: Act. Sgt. Steve Trahan testified Monday in the inquest of the 2018 death of 43-year-old Gordon Dale Couvrette
article: Lillian Couvrette wants to know whether her 43-year-old son was in handcuffs when North Bay police Tasered him on Feb. 22, 2018.
The mother of two had the opportunity to question Acting Sgt. Steven Trahan of the North Bay Police Service during Monday's inquest into the death of her son - Gordon Dale Couvrette.
Trahan was inside the three-bedroom townhouse on Feb. 22, 2018 - the day Couvrette died after being Tasered.
Trahan told Lillian Couvrette handcuffs were only placed on one side of Couvrette (around one wrist). They were not on the side of his body where Trahan was positioned.
Earlier Monday the jury heard from Couvrette's former girlfriend who said he was handcuffed when Const. Randy Adair deployed the taser.
The jury heard Adair will not be testifying. No explanation was given.
Trahan said he will never forget the events that unfolded on Feb. 22, 2018.
In his 22-year policing career it was the first and only time someone has died in his custody.
Trahan testified Monday during the inquest into the death of Couvrette.
Trahan explained to the five-member jury in detail how the events unfolded that day.

Trahan went into detail about responding to the domestic call, walking up the stairs alongside Adair and opening the bedroom door to see a woman "obviously assaulted and seeing another individual losing control of himself."
As they opened the door, Trahan said Couvrette was screaming "satanic stuff and there was obvious signs of stress."
"When we entered the room, Dale, was yelling at us 'f$#^ you pigs. I'm going to kill you," Trahan recounted.
He said he tried to handcuff the suspect, however recalled him having "superhuman strength" which made it difficult to gain control of his arms.
Trahan said what made it even more challenging is that he was covered in alcohol from Couvrette knocking over a table with liquor on it.
"It was tough to control him. My hands were slipping and I was losing my grip. We were losing control," he said.
Trahan said Adair told him and Couvrette he would be deploying his Taser.

He said he heard the Taser activate, "but as I looked at the individual on the floor it didn't faze him. His eyes didn't close. He was still yelling. It was like the Taser had no effect on this person."
But then everything changed.
Trahan said Couvrette's skin went from purple to grey to eventually black.
He said the officers got Couvrette to sit up.
"Because of his skin colour I asked Const. (Sarah) Marcotte to check his breathing. She confirmed he was (breathing). "
Trahan said he asked Marcotte a second time about Couvrette's breathing, because "he didn't look good."
They decided to take the handcuffs off and tried to communicate with Couvrette, but his eyes remained closed.
Trahan said he did a sternum rubs to see if that would open his eyes.
"Usually we get some sort of response."
But there was nothing.
Police radioed for EMS.
Trahan said he performed another sternum rub and Adair checked for a pulse on Couvrette's wrist but couldn't find one.
Trahan started CPR and testified that he continued until EMS arrived on scene.
The inquest continues today at the Best Western Hotel and Conference Centre.
